the method of successive substitutions or the Chinese Remainder Theorem. We need to solve
the system of congruences: \( x \equiv 5 \ (\text{mod} \ 8) \), \( x \equiv 1 \
(\text{mod} \ 3) \), and \( x \equiv 7 \ (\text{mod} \ 11) \). Starting with the first two
congruences, we can express \( x \) in terms of \( k \) as \( x = 8 k + 5 \), and then
substitute into the second congruence to find \( k \). Iterating through values leads to
the solution \( x = 103 \) which also satisfies the third condition. Thus, the smallest
positive integer that satisfies all three conditions is 103.
